Sri Lanka storm to third consecutive victory at Asian Netball Championship | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:05
-     - 3

by Hishan Welmilla

Sri Lanka continued their impressive campaign at the Asian Netball Championship 2026 with a commanding 78-33 victory over the Maldives, recording their third consecutive win in the tournament.

The Sri Lankan team produced another dominant performance from the opening whistle, controlling the game in all four quarters and leaving the Maldives with little opportunity to challenge their superiority.

Sri Lanka established their authority immediately, taking a 19-9 lead at the end of the first quarter. Their attacking combinations were sharp, and their defensive structure effectively restricted the Maldivian shooters, allowing Sri Lanka to build an early 10-goal advantage.

The second quarter saw Sri Lanka move into another gear. They added an impressive 26 goals, while the Maldives managed only 11, giving Sri Lanka a commanding 45-20 lead at halftime. The Sri Lankan attack continued to demonstrate excellent movement and accuracy, while their defensive players maintained relentless pressure on the opposition.

Sri Lanka were even more dominant in the third quarter. The Maldivian attack struggled to penetrate the Sri Lankan defence, scoring just three goals, while Sri Lanka added another 16 to their tally. At the end of the third quarter, Sri Lanka had extended their advantage to 61-23.

The final quarter saw Sri Lanka maintain their intensity. They scored a further 17 goals, with the Maldives managing 10, eventually sealing a comprehensive 78-33 victory.

The win further strengthens Sri Lanka’s position in the tournament following a series of contrasting results. After suffering a 67-51 defeat to Singapore, Sri Lanka drew 57-57 with hosts Hong Kong before recovering strongly to launch an impressive winning run.

Their resurgence began with a 66-53 victory over Malaysia, followed by an outstanding 100-34 demolition of India. They then continued their winning momentum against the Maldives with another emphatic performance.

The victory over India was particularly impressive, as Sri Lanka became the first team in their current campaign to reach the 100-goal mark. Their latest success against the Maldives once again demonstrated the depth and consistency of the Sri Lankan squad.

Sri Lanka’s campaign has therefore featured a mixture of adversity and remarkable recovery. The defeat to Singapore and the draw against Hong Kong were followed by three successive victories, showing the team’s ability to adapt and respond under pressure.

With their confidence growing with every match, Sri Lanka will now look to carry this momentum into the next stage of the competition. The combination of strong defensive pressure, accurate shooting and effective teamwork has made them one of the teams to watch as the Asian Netball Championship 2026 progresses.

The comprehensive victory over the Maldives not only added more points to Sri Lanka’s campaign but also underlined their determination to challenge for the Asian title. After a difficult start, the Sri Lankan side has now found its rhythm at a crucial stage of the tournament.

Sri Lanka 78-33 Maldives

Quarter scores: 19-9, 26-11, 16-3, 17-10

title: Resounding wins for Army SC, Navy SC | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:03
-     - 0

The two services teams Navy SC and Army SC registered resounding wins on the opening day of the Tier B T20 tournament on Tuesday.

Navy SC thumped Galle CC by 10 wickets at SLLDC grounds, Kirimandala. Galle CC were routed for 76 by the seam and spin of Thimira Malshan (3/17) and Ishan Abeysekera (3/14). Navy SC knocked the required runs in 6.2 overs. Adeesha Nanayakkara contributed the bulk of it with 53* off 22 balls (4 fours, 5 sixes).

Army SC beat Kandy Customs SC by 69 runs at Air Force grounds, Katunayake. Batting first Army SC ran up 201-6 courtesy fifties from Ashan Sudarshana (50 off 32 balls, 4 fours, 3 sixes) and Manushka Samith (51 off 32 balls, 3 fours, 3 sixes) and bowled out Kandy Customs SC for 132 where only the captain Yashoda Mendis made any impression with the bat – 55 off 32 balls (6 fours, 2 sixes) against the spin of Shehada Zoysa (4/28) and Janaka Sampath (3/16).

Chilaw Marians CC hit up the highest total of the day – 214-5 in their 31-run win over Kurunegala SC at Air Force grounds, Katunayake. Skipper Kasun Vidura (59 off 44 balls, 6 fours, 2 sixes) and Arosha Sithumina (79 off 44 balls, 8 fours, 4 sixes) provided the base for the total with an opening stand of 122 off 77 balls. Kurunegala SC were restricted to a total of 183-9 by the spin and seam of Thimira Irushika (3/20) and Kevin Samuel (3/42). Keshan Wanniarachchi’s 45 off 27 was the top score of their innings.

Leo CC and Ragama CC had a fight on their hands before winning. Romesh Suranga played a match-winning knock of 64* off 53 balls (4 fours, 4 sixes) to help Leo CC beat Negombo CC by 3 wickets at Welisara. Chasing Negombo CC’s score of 137-8, Leo CC lost seven wickets for 108 before clinching victory with an over to spare.

At the same venue Ragama CC pulled off a four-wicket win against Sebastianites. Sebastianites made 147 with Chamindu Perera scoring 43 off 29. Ragama CC were powered at the top by Manisha Rupasinghe (52 off 39 balls, 5 fours, 2 sixes) and then it was left to Maleesha Silva (19*) to guide them home in partnerships of 28, 27 and 16*.

The Moratuwa SC-United Southern SC game at SLLDC grounds, Kirimandala ended in a no-result with rain curtailing play. Moratuwa SC scored 164-8 and United Southern SC chasing a revised target of 113 made 21-2. – [ST]

Cristiano Ronaldo marries long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:00
-     - 6

Football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has married his longtime partner - model and influencer Georgina Rodríguez - in a civil ceremony in Portugal.

The Portuguese striker posted an image on his Instagram account showing two hands - presumed to be his on top of his wife’s - both wearing wedding rings.

Calling it the wedding of the year, Portuguese media say the couple tied the knot on 11 August in the coastal town of Cascais near Lisbon - and that their five children attended.

The Instagram entry had more than 3m likes within 30 minutes of being posted.

The couple have been together for 10 years, after they met at a Gucci shop in Madrid where Rodríguez was working. He was playing at the Spanish club Real Madrid at the time.

They announced their engagement on 11 August last year.

At the time, Rodríguez posted a picture of a large ring, writing “Yes I do. In this and in all my lives” in her native Spanish.

Ronaldo has scored nearly 1,000 goals in a career in which he has played for Lisbon-based Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus, Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia and Portugal.

He recently played in his sixth World Cup, a record for appearances in the men’s finals which he shares with Lionel Messi of Argentina.

title: Largest-ever Japanese delegation is set to visit Sri Lanka under ‘Little Japan’ initiative | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:08
-     - 3

By Uma Chandrasiri

Sri Lanka’s first ever fully Japanese funded transit hotel, the Colombo International Airport Hotel, is gearing to welcome over 250 visitors from Japan end of August this year, ranging from potential investors to tourists, as the largest ever group to tour the island. 

It is an ambitious bid by the hotels’ founder and the visionary behind ‘Little Japan’- a bilateral cultural initiative between Japan and Sri Lanka, Dr. Ruwan Perera, to strengthen ties between the two nations and promote Sri Lanka as a foremost tourist attraction to the Japanese. This program is organised under the campaign banner ‘Japan returns to Sri Lanka’.

Addressing the media at the Colombo International Airport Hotel (CIAH) recently, Rowelmark Group of Companies and CIAH Chairman Dr. Ruwan Perera explained that the idea of ‘Little Japan’, his bold and optimistic initiative to restore the somewhat neglected bilateral relations between his motherland and his current home Japan, was conceived seven years ago. 

“Little Japan is a vision and not merely a target or a milestone with a timeline attached to it. Our late president J.R. Jayawardena earned great respect from the Japanese people which resulted in the creation of strong ties between the nations and increased Japanese cooperation. My dream is to bring back the honour, respect and the bonds between the nations that have slowly eroded with time. This visit by the 250 plus Japanese delegates is merely a start, I wish to increase the delegation size to close to a thousand next year”

“Little Japan is a bilateral bridge that enhances relations between Japan and Sri Lanka” said Rowelmark Group of Companies Chief Executive Officer-leisure, Saman Perera whose main focus is to direct investments channeled through the ‘Little Japan’ initiative, toward fostering the hospitality industry and tourism promotion in Sri Lanka. “The present-day Japanese traveller seeks authentic, safe and meaningful experiences along with the rich cultural heritage and the natural beauty of a destination which Sri Lanka has in abundance. What we lack is a strong bilateral relationship and this is what we seek to recreate through our work with ‘Little Japan’”. 

Speaking about the Colombo International Airport Hotel, he added, "Our vision for CIAH is to set a benchmark in the hospitality industry as the leading transit hotel in Sri Lanka and we are confident of achieving this goal having secured over a 75% occupancy within the first quarter of the opening.”

The 5-star rated and 153 roomed Colombo International Airport Hotel, built on a site area of 31.5 acres and in very close proximity to the Bandaranaike International Airport, offers its guests a choice of exclusive eateries including a plush rooftop restaurant, a bar, swimming pool, gymnasium and spa, meeting rooms as well as a dedicated airline crew lounge.

The ‘Little Japan’ initiative has succeeded in garnering a multitude of Japanese investment into Sri Lanka, the most significant being the $ 40 million funded, Colombo International Airport Hotel. Furthermore, Dr Perera and his dedicated team have built a strong bridge to foster tourism and a sense of community between the two countries with initiatives such as the Japan Expo in 2018 and 2019, a Japanese festival in 2020, hosting a 100-member group of Japanese mothers to tour the island and hosting a 45 member business delegation in 2025. 

Extending his dream and vision to repay his motherland, Dr Perera with the backing of ‘Little Japan’, has helped develop over 50 schools across the island and sponsored Sri Lankan students to study nursing care in Japan. He also plans to sponsor deserving school and university students for a week or two long stays in Japan with the aim of gifting them with valuable life lessons as well as opportunities to gain practical knowledge that may currently be lacking in local curriculums. Furthermore, Dr. Perera has secured over Rs. 10 million and 800 kilograms of essential medicines to the Colombo General Hospital through donations from Japanese philanthropists, including doctors and nurses who have visited Sri Lanka during the Covid pandemic.

Dr. Perera believes that the Japanese manufacturers view the Indian market as a highly viable option and that they could conduct market testing in Sri Lanka initially, in order to gain a foothold into India. When questioned as to the Sri Lankan Governments’ involvement in his projects, Dr. Perera confirmed that assistance is received but that these endeavors should not merely be the responsibility of a Government but all of its citizens, stating that “Sri Lanka is not only its Government, it’s all of her people”.

Having moved to Japan for studies 30 years ago, Perera, a PhD holder in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from the prestigious University of Tokyo and the University of California, Berkeley, has dedicated his career towards fostering cooperation between the two nations and promoting economic growth in Sri Lanka. He is the Chief Envoy for Japan-Sri Lanka foreign employment relations and the Chief Representative for Japan at the Ayurvedic and Indigenous Medicine Ministry.

title: Women-only adventure challenge Raid Amazones 26th edition in Kalutara in November | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:06
-     - 3

By Saesha Basnayake

The Raid Amazones, a women-only adventure challenge, is set to hold its 26th edition in Kalutara from 2–10 November 2026, with Turyaa Kalutara serving as the base for the event. 

The challenge will bring 250 international participants to Sri Lanka to take part in activities including cycling, canoeing and trail running, while also immersing themselves in local experiences such as cricket and Sri Lankan cookery. Participants will also take part in CSR initiatives in local schools.

The Raid Amazones is no stranger to Sri Lanka, having held eight previous editions across different regions, including the Eastern Province and the Cultural Triangle. Sri Lanka has hosted more Raid Amazones editions than any other country since the event was first established in 2001. 

Connaissance de Ceylon Director of Marketing and Business Development Maxine Wickramasinghe said the aim is to “showcase the best of Sri Lanka”. This has been achieved by introducing participants to the country’s diverse landscapes and communities through each edition.

Raid Amazones founder Alexandre Debanne reflected on the decision to continue returning to Sri Lanka, stating that “the country has huge potential”. Each visit has offered the organisers the opportunity to explore different parts of the island, providing new landscapes and settings for the adventure challenges.

The decision to select Kalutara as the base for the 2026 edition was driven by the diversity of its surroundings. The region encompasses mangrove plantations, villages, paddy fields, tea, palm oil and coconut plantations. Maxine Wickramasinghe described the variety found in Kalutara as “second to none”, providing European participants with an experience that differs from previous editions.

The event is also expected to bring benefits to Kalutara itself. 

Deputy Tourism Minister Prof. Ruwan Ranasinghe described the area as “a place we need to rejuvenate”. With previous editions of the Raid Amazones reaching a global audience of more than one million people, the 2026 edition is expected to generate more than $50 million in media value. This international exposure has the potential to place Sri Lanka and Kalutara in the global spotlight while supporting the country’s wider tourism industry.

Beyond the sporting element, the Raid Amazones is centred on empowering ordinary women and encouraging them to step outside their comfort zones. Debanne explained that the event deliberately focuses on selecting the “women next door”, emphasising that the Raid Amazones is not solely about competition or travel, but about the experience participants gain along the way.

“The message was not sports or travel, it was experience,” Debanne said.

Through this approach, the Raid Amazones offer European participants an opportunity to experience Sri Lanka beyond its conventional tourist attractions, while simultaneously showcasing the country’s landscapes, culture and communities to an international audience.

Acorn Group brings next-generation airline booking technology to Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 13 August 2026 00:00
-     - 2

Acorn Group, has been appointed General Sales Agent (GSA) in Sri Lanka for Iris, the airline retailing platform developed by Dubai-based TPConnects Technologies. 

The appointment gives travel agencies across the country access to the latest airline booking and retailing technology through a single platform.

As the GSA, Acorn Ventures will bring TPConnects’ advanced airline retailing platform to travel agencies across the country. Iris provides unified access to content from more than 60 NDC and low-cost carrier sources, as well as all four major GDSs, through a single interface

The platform enables faster shopping, access to private and negotiated fares, richer airline content including ancillaries and bundled offers, intelligent pricing, and streamlined post-booking servicing. With flexible payment controls, rapid deployment, and an intuitive user interface, Iris helps travel agencies improve efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and accelerate business growth.

Acorn Group Aviation Sector Partner and Chairperson Dushy Jayaweera said:  “As Sri Lanka’s travel industry continues its strong recovery, travel agents need richer airline content, faster shopping experiences and greater control over the booking journey. Iris allows us to meet those expectations, and our established presence and deep relationships with travel agencies across the country position us to deliver real value through this platform.”

TPConnects Technologies CEO Eric Dumas said: “Sri Lanka’s travel market represents a significant opportunity, with travel sellers seeking modern airline content solutions that don’t add operational complexity. Acorn Group’s market leadership, extensive distribution network and trusted reputation make them the ideal partner to introduce Iris to Sri Lanka.”

Sri Lanka’s travel industry is experiencing robust growth, with rising outbound demand and a recovering inbound tourism sector. The partnership positions local travel sellers to capitalise on these opportunities with tools that enhance competitiveness, improve margins and deliver a better customer experience.
